provisions.summary: Keeps the state refundable earned income tax credit at 40% of the federal credit ("unless otherwise provided by law") and, via Section 3, preserves this amendment to section 235-55.75(a) when the subsection is reenacted on December 31, 2027, so the 40% rate continues past 2027.
provisions.quote: the tax credit, for the appropriate taxable year, shall be forty per cent of the federal earned income tax credit allowed

provisions.summary: Extends the earned income tax credit to nonresidents and requires part-year residents and nonresidents to multiply the credit by the ratio of Hawaii AGI to federal AGI. The model covers resident households only, so this cannot be expressed.
provisions.quote: For a part-year resident[,] or a nonresident, the tax credit shall equal the amount of the tax credit calculated in subsection (a) multiplied by the ratio of Hawaii adjusted gross income to federal adjusted gross income.

provisions.summary: Ends the carryforward of nonrefundable earned income tax credits claimed for tax year 2022: none may be used in a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2025. The model has no credit carryforwards.
provisions.quote: shall be used as a credit for a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2025.

notes: The effective date of July 1, 3000 looks like a placeholder, and the bill applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. The spec is set to first_year 2027, the first modeled year. Section 3 preserves only the amendments to section 235-55.75(a), so only eitc_percent is set. The bill does not mention section 235-55.85(b), so food_excise is left out and Act 163's larger food/excise table still ends after tax year 2027 under current law. The 40% rate is explicit in the amended subsection (a) text. The nonresident clarification and the 2022 carryforward cutoff are not modeled.
